Kasımpaşa’s Lightning Start The game began in explosive fashion as the visitors stunned the home crowd almost immediately. With only one minute on the clock, Fousseni Diabate provided a clinical assist for Adrian Benedyczak , who clinicaly slotted home the opening goal. The situation went from bad to worse for Gençlerbirliği in the 12th minute when the referee pointed to the penalty spot. Adrian Benedyczak stepped up once more, converting the spot-kick with composure to give Kasımpaşa a commanding two-goal lead early on. Faced with an uphill battle, the hosts made an early tactical switch, bringing on Cihan Canak for Sekou Koita after just 14 minutes. The intensity of the match rose quickly, leading to early yellow cards for Zan Zuzek and Franco Tongya as both sides fought for control of the midfield. The Momentum Shifts Before the Break Just as it looked like Kasımpaşa would head into the locker room with a comfortable lead, Gençlerbirliği found a lifeline. In the 42nd minute, Ogulcan Ulgun set up Adama Traore , who finished with precision to make it 1-2. The home side wasn't finished there; deep into first-half stoppage time (45+4'), Metehan Mimaroglu delivered a cross for Dimitrios Goutas , who powered a strike home to equalize and complete a stunning first-half recovery. Penalty Drama and Late Chaos The second half was a tighter affair, characterized by tactical fouls and mounting pressure. The decisive moment arrived in the 71st minute when Gençlerbirliği were awarded a penalty of their own. Franco Tongya held his nerve to beat the keeper, turning the game completely on its head at 3-2. Kasımpaşa attempted to fight back, introducing Cafu and Cenk Tosun , but their frustrations grew as the clock ticked down. The closing stages were marred by a flurry of disciplinary actions. Kerem Demirbay , Rodrigo Becão , and Cenk Tosun were all cautioned as tempers flared. In a chaotic 12 minutes of added time, the referee handed out further yellow cards to Adem Arous , Andreas Gianniotis , and Adrian Benedyczak , but Gençlerbirliği held firm to secure all three points in a classic encounter.

The Süper Lig clash between Kasımpaşa and Kocaelispor on May 3, 2026, promised a tactical battle as both sides looked to establish their dominance in a high-stakes encounter. With vital points at stake, the atmosphere at the stadium was electric as the referee blew the opening whistle to signal the start of an intense afternoon of football. A Lightning Start for the Hosts The match ignited almost immediately after kickoff, caught in a whirlwind of home-side pressure. In just the second minute, Kasımpaşa tore through the opposition defense to find the opening goal . Mortadha Ben Ouanes proved to be the architect, delivering a precise pass to Adrian Benedyczak , who made no mistake in clinical fashion, sending the home crowd into raptures. This early breakthrough set a frantic tone for the first half , where the hosts looked significantly hungrier and more organized than their visitors, winning almost every second ball. Kocaelispor struggled to find any sort of rhythm as the home side continued to apply high-intensity pressure across the pitch. That persistence paid off again in the 23rd minute when Serdar Dursun turned provider, spotting a gap in the defensive line to find Daniel Agyei . Agyei capitalized on the service with a composed finish to double the advantage, leaving the visitors with a mountain to climb before the half-hour mark. Despite a few desperate attempts to regroup before the interval, Kocaelispor entered the break trailing by two after a dominant display from the Kasımpaşa frontline. Tactical Discipline and Closing the Door The second half saw a more disciplined approach from both sides as the intensity shifted from attacking flair to tactical management. Kocaelispor ’s frustration began to manifest on the hour mark; in the 58th minute, Ahmet Oguz received a yellow card following a mistimed challenge as he tried to halt a counter-attack. Managerial shifts followed shortly after as both benches looked to influence the game's momentum. Rigoberto Rivas replaced the cautioned Oguz to provide a fresh spark for the visitors, while Kasımpaşa introduced Tayfur Bingol for Joseph Boende to solidify their midfield control. As the match entered its final phase, Kasımpaşa focused on defensive solidity, utilizing their bench to maintain energy levels and prevent any late chance for a comeback. Late substitutions saw the goal-scorer Daniel Agyei and Claudio Winck make way for Furkan Gedik and Godfried Frimpong as the clock ticked toward the 90th minute. Despite five minutes of added time being signaled by the fourth official, the visitors could not find a way through the organized backline. The referee’s final whistle confirmed a professional and decisive performance, securing all three points for a resurgent Kasımpaşa side.
